summary: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot() overwrote an existing destination session file with the colliding legacy source. Repair adds an existsSync(newPath) guard that skips the move, preserving both copies while unrelated legacy files still migrate.

changes.description: Skip the rename when the destination file already exists so the existing destination and the colliding legacy source are both left untouched; the loop continues with other files.

Standalone dependency-free Node assertion script that drives the real migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot through subject.mjs with a caller-owned temporary agentDir and asserts destination bytes, legacy source bytes, and continued migration of unrelated files.

claims.claim: The production collision guard now skips an existing destination instead of renaming over it, and the surrounding loop iteration continues with the remaining files.
The regression asserts the existing destination keeps its exact original bytes after migration.
The regression asserts the colliding legacy source still exists at the agent root with its original bytes and that no extra copy is produced.
The regression asserts unrelated legacy files still migrate byte-for-byte, including a case where only the destination directory pre-exists.
The regression runs the real production code loaded by the read-only subject helper with explicit getAgentDir/stripBom boundary fakes and real fs/path.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0 (stripTypeScriptTypes + vm.SourceTextModule, no node_modules or network used). Fixed tree: exit 0, prints 'session migration collision policy: OK'. Differential control: reinstating the original fault (removing the existsSync(newPath) guard so renameSync overwrites the destination) produced exit 1 with targeted assertion failures -- 'existing destination was overwritten by the colliding legacy source', 'colliding legacy source was moved or deleted', and 'destination mutated on rerun' -- while the unrelated-migration and free-slot migration checks still passed, proving the failure was the collision policy and not a load/timeout error. Restoring the fix returns exit 0. The temporary agentDir is created under .prale-eval/ and removed in a finally block, so no residue is left behind. The repository's vitest/tsc suites were not run because dependencies are not installed; the VM regression is the exercised validation.
